name: A10G
notes: gpu_chip of GA102 is NOT stated in the AWS-published A10G datasheet used as this record's primary source (only 'NVIDIA Ampere architecture' is given there) and is NOT the same as blindly carrying over A10's die by assumption -- it is instead independently corroborated by a third-party GPU database (sysrqmts.com) that explicitly names BOTH 'NVIDIA A10 PCIe' and 'NVIDIA A10G' as sharing GPU model 'GA102', specifically variant 'GA102-890-A1', in a side-by-side comparison. This is real (if non-NVIDIA-primary) evidence that the two parts share silicon despite their throughput differences -- recorded with the same 'corroborated, not NVIDIA-confirmed' caveat as process_node_nm below, not asserted with full confidence. process_node_nm of 8 (Samsung 8nm '8N') carries the identical caveat -- not found in any NVIDIA document, corroborated only by the same sysrqmts.com comparison plus independent A10-specific sources (see gpus/a10.json). release_date of 2021-11-11 reflects AWS's own blog/NVIDIA developer blog announcement of EC2 G5 general availability (A10G's actual public debut); a closely-adjacent AWS 'What's New' catalog entry lists 2021-11-12 for the same event -- treated as the same announcement with a 1-day discrepancy likely from timezone/publish-time artifacts, not two separate events. This date is genuinely different from and later than NVIDIA's own A10 announcement (2021-04-12, see gpus/a10.json) -- confirming A10G was announced roughly 7 months after A10, as a distinct AWS-specific product debut, not simultaneously. A10G is AWS's own EC2 SKU, distinct from NVIDIA's own-branded A10 (see gpus/a10.json) -- confirmed via an official AWS-published NVIDIA datasheet (d1.awsstatic.com), not merely AWS's marketing page. This resolves an earlier ambiguity in this dataset: A10G is NOT a renamed/relabeled A10, it is a genuinely different part with a higher TDP (300W vs A10's 150W) and 80 RT cores vs A10's 72 (RT core count corroborated by AWS's separately-published EC2 G5 instance-type page). HOWEVER, despite the higher TDP and RT core count, A10G's Tensor Core throughput is LOWER than A10's at every precision except plain FP32 vector: TF32/BF16/FP16/INT8 dense figures on A10G are roughly HALF of A10's (e.g. TF32 dense 35 vs A10's 62.5; INT8 dense 140 vs A10's 250), while FP32 vector is slightly higher on A10G (35 vs 31.2). This is counterintuitive for a higher-TDP part and worth flagging: on every other Ampere GPU in this dataset (A10, A100), TF32 dense throughput is exactly 2x FP32 vector throughput -- but on A10G, TF32 dense (35) EQUALS FP32 (35), breaking that pattern. Both figures are taken verbatim from the official AWS-published datasheet and are internally self-consistent (the ~0.56x ratio holds uniformly across TF32/BF16/FP16/INT8), so this is recorded as-is rather than assumed to be a typo, but it remains an open oddity worth re-verifying against another primary source if precision matters for your use case. No FP64 or FP8 figures given (FP8 Tensor Core postdates Ampere; FP64 simply not listed on this consumer/inference-oriented datasheet). INT4 Tensor Core is also given (280 TOPS dense | 560 TOPS sparse) but not recorded as a separate field since this schema has no int4 field -- noted here for reference. cuda_cores/tensor_cores/sm_count not stated numerically anywhere on this datasheet (Tensor Core generation given by name only: 'third-generation'). No NVLink (PCIe-only, 2-slot FHFL card). multi_instance_max left null -- MIG support not mentioned on this datasheet either way; not assumed absent or present.

_sources.rt_core_generation: https://d1.awsstatic.com/product-marketing/ec2/NVIDIA_AWS_A10G_DataSheet_FINAL_02_17_2022.pdf ('second-generation RT Cores' body text; the spec table itself gives count only, not generation)
_sources.gpu_chip: Not NVIDIA-primary-sourced -- sysrqmts.com GPU comparison page names both A10 and A10G as GPU model 'GA102', variant 'GA102-890-A1'
_sources.process_node_nm: Not NVIDIA-primary-sourced -- same sysrqmts.com comparison ('Foundry: Samsung / Manufacturing process: 8 nm', stated for both A10 and A10G)
_sources.release_date: https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/aws-brings-nvidia-a10g-tensor-core-gpus-to-the-cloud-with-new-ec2-g5-instances/ (Nov 11 2021); cross-referenced against AWS's own 'What's New' catalog entry (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2021/11/announcing-general-availability-amazon-ec2-g5-instances/) which lists Nov 12 2021 for the same EC2 G5 GA event
